metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL PostgreSQL OTel] Vacuum blocked by old transaction
metadata.description: Alerts when the age of the oldest transaction not yet vacuumed stays at or above 100 million transactions for the whole 30-minute window, per holder type (running, prepared, replication_slot, replica). This is a leading indicator of bloat and transaction ID wraparound, and the holder type says what to end or drop. The unit is a transaction count, not seconds. PostgreSQL-only metric, so no engine marker is needed. Grouped by database_id and blocker type.

data.content:
## Cloud SQL PostgreSQL vacuum blocked by an old transaction

Something has held back the vacuum horizon for at least 100 million transactions. Vacuum cannot remove dead rows or freeze transaction IDs newer than it.

### Triage by `blocker_type`
- `running`: a long-running or `idle in transaction` session. Find it with `SELECT pid, usename, state, xact_start, backend_xmin FROM pg_stat_activity ORDER BY age(backend_xmin) DESC NULLS LAST;` and terminate it if safe.
- `prepared`: an orphaned two-phase transaction in `pg_prepared_xacts`. Commit or roll it back.
- `replication_slot`: an inactive or lagging logical/physical slot in `pg_replication_slots`. Drop it if unused. It also retains WAL and fills the disk.
- `replica`: a read replica with `hot_standby_feedback` running long queries.

Then check transaction ID utilization and disk utilization for the same instance.

### Tuning
- The threshold is in transactions, so its meaning depends on write rate. Lower it for low-throughput instances, where an hours-old transaction may only be a few million transactions old.
